items.title: Library book procurement scam: Madras HC tells DVAC to file FIR
items.summary: A contempt of court petition was filed before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday, November 10, alleging disobedience of a June 2024 order that directed the Tamil Nadu government to ensure transparency in the procurement of books for public libraries. Hearing the matter, a Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register an FIR into alleged fraudulent practices and sought the names of officials responsible for the procurement irregularities. Justice GR Swaminathan, who was part of the Bench that passed the original order along with Justice R Mahadevan (now a Supreme Court judge), told the newly appointed Director of Public Libraries, RV Shajeevana, that the matters that had recently come to light amounted to "blatant disobedience" of the court's directions. The judge said the Bench intended to take the matter very seriously. The judges said the fraudulent practices in the procurement of books for public libraries had been uncovered following an article written by Tamil author Perumal Murugan. items.title: No plans to allot Central Secretariat Club premises to anyone at this stage: Centre to Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Central government has informed the Delhi High Court that there is no proposal to allot the Central Secretariat Club premises to anyone at this stage. Central Government Standing Counsel (CGSC) Radhika Bishwajit Dubey made the statement before Justice Amit Mahajan on November 5 during the hearing of an application filed by the Club seeking stay on the government’s order of de-recognition and eviction of the club. “Ms Radhika Bishwajit Dubey, learned CGSC for the respondents, on instructions, submits that there is no proposal to allot the subject premises to any party at this stage. Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The petitioners are permitted to take away their belongings in next one week,” the Court said in its order. The case will be heard next on December 21. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The application was filed by the Club in its already pending case challenging the de-recognition and the eviction order. It stated that the government was in the process of handing over possession of the land to RML Hospital, "thereby confronting this Hon’ble Court with a completed fait accompli" before its petition could be heard. items.title: Bombay High Court quashes Customs order flagged for citing non-existent AI-generated judgments
items.summary: The Bombay High Court recently set aside a customs department order after taking note of concerns that the adjudicating authority had relied on non-existent, artificial intelligence (AI) generated Supreme Court judgments [ Quanta Logistics Pvt Ltd v. Commissioner of Customs (Import-I) ]. A Bench of Justices MS Karnik and Sandesh D Patil quashed an August 11, 2026 order passed by the customs commissioner against Quanta Logistics. Justice MS Karnik, Justice Sandesh Patil Quanta argued that the customs authority passed the order by resorting to AI without an independent application of mind. Senior Advocate Venkatesh Dhond demonstrated that the order cited two Supreme Court judgments that did not exist in any database, describing them as possible AI hallucinations. When Quanta requested for copies of the cited judgment, the department failed to provide the same. Senior Advocate Venkatesh Dhond The petitioner relied on the 2026 Supreme Court decision in Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya v. Union of India, in which the apex court had emphasised on a "zero-tolerance" approach to tackling the use of AI-generated precedents without due verification.
